title: Brain to cord on BANC v888, with the weight per synapse calibrated to BANC's synapse density
source: Bates et al. 2026, Nature, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10735-w (BANC v888; data CC BY 4.0, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/7WTH1N); model: Shiu et al. 2024, Nature 634:210-219, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07763-9
preregistration: Written after the dev run of banc-cord-v888.json (4 of 10 criteria; MN9 silent even for labellar sugar) and before any run of this file. Conditions, seeds, readouts and criteria are banc-cord-v888.json's, unchanged; the one difference is w_syn, fixed by a structural rule chosen before any run with it: Shiu et al. set w_syn by hand (0.275 mV) for FAFB v783, whose network gives a neuron 391.32 synapses on average (54,492,922 synapses over 139,255 neurons); Codex's BANC export gives 148.84 (23,556,214 over 158,262), partly because it omits pairs of fewer than 3 synapses. Scaling w_syn by 391.32 / 148.84 = 2.629 gives a BANC neuron the same mean synaptic drive per neuron as Shiu et al.'s network: 0.275 x 2.629 = 0.7230 mV. No other value was tried. Both files' held-out runs are reported. The rest, from the original file: criteria, rates, trial counts and seeds were written before any simulation on BANC v888 (only its neuron counts, populations and synapse counts between named cell types had been read). Dev seeds may be run while the code changes; held-out seeds are run once, on the commit that is reported, and their result is reported whatever it is. Thresholds marked 'ours' are not from a paper. The model has no gap junctions: the giant fiber's electrical synapses onto TTMn and PSI are absent, and only their chemical synapses (13 and 15 in this export) are in the graph; B5, B6 and B8 test whether the cord carries the giant fiber's spike anyway, and are reported whatever they show. Codex's BANC table lists pairs of 3 or more synapses only (FAFB's lists all), and Shiu et al.'s parameters are used unrefitted.

protocol.notes: Shiu et al.'s defaults: 30 trials of 1000 ms, Poisson input at the stated rate to every neuron of the stimulated population. Populations are rules over BANC v888's own annotations (populations.py, banc_*), both sides together; signs are each neuron's predicted transmitter (banc.py).

criteria.claim: Sugar on the legs drives the proboscis motor neuron MN9, through the ventral nerve cord
criteria.quote: stimulation of the tarsi with sugar elicits proboscis extension (Dethier 1976); the legs' Gr5a neurons project to the thoracic ganglia (Wang et al. 2004)
criteria.threshold_note: active = MN9 fires at least once in the trial; in at least half the trials (ours: no paper states a rate for this pathway)

criteria.claim: Shuffling the connectome's weights abolishes leg-sugar-evoked MN9 activation
criteria.quote: only 1 of 100 shuffled simulations did (Shiu et al., for labellar sugar)

criteria.claim: Labellar sugar GRNs at 100 Hz activate MN9 in every simulation, in a second animal's connectome
criteria.quote: modelling using the correct connectome results in robust activation of MN9 in 100% of simulations when sugar-sensing neurons are activated at 100 Hz (Shiu et al., FAFB)
criteria.threshold_note: as S1 of shiu2024-v783; BANC's labellar sugar GRNs of both sides, not Shiu et al.'s one-sided set

criteria.claim: Bitter GRN activity inhibits sugar-evoked MN9 firing, in a second animal's connectome
criteria.quote: the addition of bitter GRN activity to sugar GRN activation in our model resulted in an inhibition of MN6 and MN9 (Shiu et al.)

criteria.claim: A giant-fiber spike train drives the jump motor neuron TTMn
criteria.quote: the giant fiber drives TTMn, the jump muscle's motor neuron, and through PSI the DLM flight motor neurons (King & Wyman 1980); a giant-fiber spike selects the short-mode takeoff (von Reyn et al. 2014)
criteria.threshold_note: TTMn fires at least once in nearly every trial (ours); the electrical synapse that carries most of this in the fly is absent from the model

criteria.claim: A giant-fiber spike train drives the DLM wing power motor neurons
criteria.quote: the giant fiber drives TTMn, the jump muscle's motor neuron, and through PSI the DLM flight motor neurons (King & Wyman 1980)
criteria.threshold_note: ours; GF to PSI is electrical in the fly and only 15 chemical synapses here, while PSI to the DLM motor neurons is chemical

criteria.claim: Looming input to LPLC2 and LC4 drives the giant fiber
criteria.quote: LC4 encodes angular velocity and LPLC2 angular size, and both converge on the giant fiber (von Reyn et al. 2017; Ache et al. 2019)
criteria.threshold_note: the giant fiber fires at least once in at least half the trials (ours)

criteria.claim: Looming input reaches the jump motor neuron, eye to leg in one connectome
criteria.quote: LC4 and LPLC2 converge on the giant fiber (von Reyn et al. 2017), which drives TTMn (King & Wyman 1980)

criteria.claim: The antennal-grooming descending neurons drive front-leg motor neurons
criteria.quote: aDN activation elicits antennal grooming, which the front legs perform (Hampel et al. 2015)
criteria.threshold_note: at least one front-leg motor neuron fires in nearly every trial (ours)

criteria.claim: The antennal-grooming descending neurons drive the front legs more than the hind legs
criteria.quote: aDN activation elicits antennal grooming, which the front legs perform (Hampel et al. 2015)
criteria.threshold_note: per-neuron rate of the front-leg motor neurons above the hind-leg ones, trial by trial (one-sided sign test over the trials that differ; ours)
